title: Run tree: orchestrator, roles and steps with live status
lead: Owner 2026-10-20 (#110, ui.run-tree): see what step is running, under the orchestrator, as a tree. The tree shows in the S26 detail pane: the orchestrator, then its roles and steps with a state glyph (running, done, failed, waiting) and a spinner on each running step, with role, vendor, model, phase and elapsed time. Data: for an engine run the roles in the run record; for a ledger run the steps with their parent (slicer relay-run list shows the nesting; relay-run step --parent). The animated flow diagram, stage bars and charts stay in S07, which builds on this tree. S30 shows the running role on a row; this slice shows the whole tree.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A row says a run is active with N steps running but not which. The owner wants to see the tree of who is doing what.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/source and internal/slicercli: the step fields the tree needs (id, parent, role, agent, vendor, model, reasoning, phase, task, times) from the ledger JSON; check the field names with slicer relay-run list --json before building.
- internal/daemon: carry the steps and the engine run's roles in the snapshot; a wire field is proposed, ask the owner if a shape beyond that is needed.
- internal/tui: the tree in the S26 pane, spinner on running steps (a tick; no goroutine in Update), tests, goldens.
- docs/dashboard.md (dash.role-detail), docs/state.md or design.md where they list the wire.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A ledger run with steps and parents renders as a tree: the orchestrator at the root, its steps beneath, children indented under their parent step.
- Each node shows a state glyph, role, model and phase; a running node shows a spinner frame that advances on a tick; a failed node is marked.
- An engine run shows its roles (implementer, reviewer, gate) as a tree under the run with the same glyphs.
- A step whose parent is unknown or missing is shown at the root, not dropped.
- A long task text is cut to fit the width; 80-column and narrow layouts keep the tree readable.
- Monochrome and colour golden views; the spinner has an ASCII fallback.
- Runs started elsewhere show the tree read-only (no actions).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Verified ledger fields: `slicer relay-run list --json --lean` gives runs[] with id, items, worktree, begun_at, updated_at, state, outcome, counts and steps. Each step has id, role, agent, vendor, model, reasoning, phase, task, parent, begun_at and updated_at. internal/slicercli/types.go:88-135 already parses them. --lean drops empty fields, so a missing parent means root. Phases in the current output: done (127) and fail (22). ork writes "start" (internal/engine/round.go:357), but no sampled run had a running step.
1. Write the failing tests first in internal/tui/runtree_test.go (new). Reuse testdata/cli/slicer/relay-run-list.json and add a tree sample.
2. internal/slicercli/types.go: Step and RelayRun need no change.
3. internal/source/source.go:67-71 and 101,133 keep active ledger runs with counts only. The wire Relay (internal/daemon/wire.go:94-104) has Steps and Running counts only. Add the step list (proposed field `tree`).
4. Engine runs with RelayRun set already have each role round as a ledger step under the orchestrator step (round.go:357). Show the ledger tree in that case. Without RelayRun, build the tree from runrec.Record.Roles (internal/runrec/record.go:47-62); RoleRecord.Step (record.go:55) links to the ledger step. Never show both.
5. Add the engine run's roles to the EngineRun wire (internal/source/source.go:154-165, built at internal/daemon/runs.go:458). Proposed fields.
6. internal/tui/pane.go: add runTreeLines(steps, width, frame) (new function), used in the pane body near pane.go:95-104.
7. Build the tree from parent ids. Children go under their parent. A missing parent goes to the root. Keep a visited set so a loop cannot hang.
8. Glyphs: phase "start" is running (spinner frame), "done" and "fail" as named. "waiting" is open (see Open).
9. Spinner: a frame index advanced by a tick message. Reuse tickMsg (internal/tui/model.go:46-47, 125-130). No goroutine in Update. Mono frames are ASCII: | / - \.
10. Clip the task text with the existing clip helper, so 80-column and narrow layouts stay readable.
11. docs/dashboard.md:206-214 (dash.role-detail): describe the tree.
12. Goldens: go test ./internal/tui -update, then review the diff in testdata/golden/ (colour and mono, 80x24 and 100x30).
Open:
- The "waiting" glyph has no source. No ledger phase or field means waiting. The owner or slicer must define it.
- The wire shape is proposed. Owner to confirm if more than the step fields are needed.
- An engine run without RelayRun has RoleRecords with no parent (record.go:47-62), so its roles render flat. This matches the item text.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- go test -race -count=1 ./internal/tui ./internal/source ./internal/daemon ./internal/slicercli
- go test -race -count=1 ./...
- go vet ./...
- gofmt -l .   (expect no output)
- go test ./internal/tui -update, then review the diff in testdata/golden/ (new tree goldens in colour and mono, 80x24 and 100x30)
- Spinner test: two tick messages change the frame; no real timer in tests.
- Ledger tests use fixtures only. No live `slicer relay-run` call.
- slicer check
- adj lint
